reason: As written the falsifier does not discriminate. (1) G2(M) and G(M) are never defined and 'permutation null' is unspecified. (2) Sampling 2^12 legs per bucket gives noise ~2^-6, but for a linear/trace or x mod M / floor(xM/p) filter on x the true bias is character-sum small (Weil/Bombieri-Deligne for psi(a.x(P+Q)+b.x(P)+c.x(Q)) on E x E), expected O(q^-1/2) = 2^-6.5..2^-9.5 at n=13..19, i.e. at or below the noise floor, so 'G2 = 1+O(noise)' is guaranteed and uninformative; it cannot separate the hypothesis from its negation. (3) 'max over 200 random + greedy best' is a selection statistic; the pool of linear filters grows with n, so a >=2x rise of the max can appear in the null; the null must use the identical selection over a matched-size pool, and the greedy filter must be scored on held-out curves. (4) No positive control, so a null result cannot be told from an insensitive instrument. (5) n=15 is composite: F_2^15 contains F_8 and F_32, so trace filters have subfield structure that contaminates a 'prime-n' scaling story (n=131 is prime). (6) Single-curve runs are confounded by cofactor/group structure. (7) '2x growth over n=13..19' is a 6-bit window; it cannot be extrapolated to n=131 without a fitted slope with a CI. The metric type is fine (structural/statistical: bias, mutual information; no wall time), CPU budget is fine, and the programme tools suffice (python3+numpy only). The experiment is fixable by replacing sampling with exact character-sum evaluation, which removes the noise problem. Scope: kills/settles only 2-valued extension for single-bit-linear and mod/floor filters on x; says nothing about non-linear algebraic filters, and the toy proves nothing about n=131 beyond a fitted exponent.
fix: REDESIGN. (A) Exact evaluation, no sampling. Pick curves whose E(F_q) has a large cyclic subgroup <g> (order N ~ 2^n); tabulate x(g^i), i<N (one sequential add loop, numpy log/exp tables for GF(2^n), or Montgomery ladder over Kummer line). For a filter pair define f_a(i)=(-1)^{a.x(g^i)} (binary, a a j-dim F_2-linear map; for prime arm use indicator of bucket floor(xM/p)=t or x mod M=t). Single-valued correlation C1(a,b,c)=sum_{i,j} f_a(i) f_b(j) f_c(i+j) = (1/N) sum_chi fhat_a fhat_b conj(fhat_c) by FFT, O(N log N), exact. Two-valued sign-ambiguous statistic uses P-Q too: C-(a,b,c)=sum f_a(i)f_b(j)f_c(i-j); the symmetric multiset observables are s_lin=f_c(i+j)+f_c(i-j) (reduces to C1 + C-, exact via FFT) and s_quad=f_c(i+j)f_c'(i-j) (not FFT-able; compute exactly by O(N^2) chunked numpy only for n<=15, Monte-Carlo with 2^28 pairs for n>=17 and report the MC standard error). (B) Define metrics up front: for j-bit filter h, I1 = I(h(P),h(Q); h(P+Q)) and I2 = I(h(P),h(Q); {h(P+Q),h(P-Q)}) in bits (from the exact joint tables for j<=4, from the Fourier spectrum sum of |C|^2 normalised for larger j), plus per-bucket gain G=max_t Pr[h(P+Q)=t | buckets]/2^-j. Report I2-I1 and G2/G jointly (is the 2-valued rule better than single-valued at all) and the log2 slope of excess bias versus n. (C) Fields: prime n only, n in {11,13,17,19,23}; drop n=15. >=6 random curves per n (include one Koblitz y^2+xy=x^3+1), j in {1,2,3,4,6,8}; prime arm p in {2^16,2^18,2^20,2^22} primes, M in {4,8,16,64,256}, both x mod M and floor(xM/p). Fix j and also fix j/n separately. (D) Null arms: (N1) random-function null: replace x(g^i) by a random permutation of the x-values multiset (preserves bucket marginals, destroys group relation); (N2) same selection procedure (200 random filters then greedy pick) run on the null, same pool size, to give the null distribution of the selected max at every n; (N3) held-out scoring: select filter on curve set A, report on curve set B. Success criteria in sigma units from N2, 5 sigma. (E) Positive controls (must pass or the run is void): (P1) group-quotient filter h(P)=±(dlog mod m) on curves with m | |E|, m in {3,5,7,8,16}; here C1 is known (G=m-ish, G2 exact on the sign-ambiguous quotient); (P2) full filter h=x (j=n) must reproduce the S_3 two-root exactness (check that {x(P+Q),x(P-Q)} equals the roots of S_3(x_P,x_Q,X) on 100% of sampled pairs, using binary S_3 (X1X2+X1X3+X2X3)^2+X1X2X3+a6 as in ffd_s3_formula_control.py). (F) Decision rule: fit log2(excess bias) = alpha*n + beta across n with 95% CI over curves. Growth (alpha>=0 with CI excluding the Weil value -1/2, and excess above N2 at 5 sigma) supports the idea; alpha consistent with -1/2 (Weil) or noise-dominated => closes the 2-valued extension of KN-OPEN-91d4f6 for linear/mod/floor filters, with the scope limited to those filter classes. Extrapolate only via the fitted alpha: at alpha=-1/2 the n=131 bias is ~2^-65, far below any Wagner level gain, so report it as a scaling statement conditional on filter class, not as a statement about all h. Budget: FFT n=23 is ~8M points, ~1 s per triple; limit triples to ~2000 total; est. 8-14 CPU-min python3+numpy. Counted/structural outputs only (bits, bias, slope); no wall-time claims.
